summary.text: Jon Bonck won the election for Texas's open 38th District on November 3, 2026, defeating Melissa McDonough, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new Congress convenes on January 3, 2027.

A Houston-area mortgage sales manager with a background in quality control and marketing in the biochemical and petroleum industries, he won the Republican nomination in a May 26, 2026 primary runoff. His campaign website describes him as a deacon and Bible study teacher at Second Baptist Church.

paragraphs.text: Bonck earned a bachelor's degree in biochemistry from Louisiana State University and worked in quality control in the biochemical and petroleum industries.
He moved into a marketing role with Nalco Champion in 2015 and became a sales manager at Bonck & Baker Mortgage Group in 2019, where he was working as of the 2026 primary.
His campaign website says he and his wife, Laura, have more than two decades of combined experience in real estate.
Bonck finished first in the 10-candidate March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 46.8% and won the May 26 runoff against Shelly deZevallos with 64.8%.
His campaign website says he serves as a deacon and Bible study teacher at Second Baptist Church.
Bonck won the November 3, 2026 general election with 51.5% of the vote to Melissa McDonough's 47.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
